questions.text: What distinguishes sliding-window attention from FlashAttention applied to full dense attention?

options.A: Both remove all long-range query–key pairs from the model.
options.B: Sliding-window attention changes allowed token pairs; FlashAttention changes how dense attention is computed.
options.C: FlashAttention changes allowed token pairs; sliding-window attention only changes memory layout.
options.D: Both replace attention weights with a uniform distribution over the prefix.

questions.explanation: Sliding-window attention restricts the attention pattern. FlashAttention tiles and reorganizes dense attention computation without removing allowed pairs.

questions.text: A model using only narrow sliding windows struggles to retrieve distant information. Which architectural change directly restores some global attention paths?

options.A: Remove positional signals from every attention layer.
options.B: Use the same narrow window in every layer and remove residuals.
options.C: Interleave sliding-window layers with full-attention layers.
options.D: Replace every attention output with the current token embedding.

questions.explanation: Interleaving global layers lets positions access distant tokens directly while retaining local attention in other layers.
At i=4 with window=3, lo=max(0,4-3+1)=2 and range(2,5) permits indices 2,3,4.
